column1: PATHOLOGY
1. The disease triangle is composed of:
A. Host, pathogen and environment   B. Host, vector and soil  C. Pathogen, soil and fertilizer
D. Host, insect and temperature
2. Pathogenicity refers to the:
A. Degree of disease produced  B. Ability of a pathogen to cause disease C. Ability of a host to resist disease D. Rate of pathogen multiplication
3. Virulence is best defined as the:
A. Ability of a pathogen to survive     B. Ability to produce spores    C. Degree of pathogenicity of a pathogen   D. Ability to enter plant tissues
4. Which of the following is a sign rather than a symptom?
A. Chlorosis    B. Wilt     C. Necrosis   D. Fungal mycelium on a diseased leaf
5. The inoculum that initiates the first infection in a crop is called:
A. Secondary inoculum   B. Primary inoculum  C. Latent inoculum  D. Residual inoculum
6. The visible expression of a plant disease is known as a:
A. Symptom   B. Sign   C. Spore   D. Inoculum
7. A disease caused by drought, salinity or nutrient imbalance is classified as:
A. Biotic disease   B. Infectious disease   C. Abiotic disorder  D. Parasitic disease
8. A pathogen that obtains nutrients from living host cells is called a:
A. Saprophyte  B. Biotroph  C. Decomposer   D. Saprobe
9. The vegetative body of most fungi is called:
A. Mycelium  B. Spore    C. Conidium     D. Sorus
10. A single fungal filament is known as a:
A. Conidium B. Sclerotium     C. Hypha    D. Sporangium
11. Which structure is commonly involved in penetration of the host surface by many fungi?
A. Appressorium  B. Sclerotium    C. Rhizomorph  D. Sporangiophore
12. Sclerotia primarily function as:
A. Reproductive structures   B. Nutrient-absorbing structures   C. Long-term survival structures    D. Penetration structures
13. Conidia are generally:
A. Sexual spores   B. Asexual spores   C. Bacterial cells    D. Nematode eggs
14. Which genus is commonly associated with vascular wilt diseases?
A. Puccinia    B. Fusarium    C. Erysiphe     D. Albugo
15. Damping-off of seedlings is commonly associated with:
A. Pythium     B. Puccinia    C. Ustilago    D. Alternaria
16. Powdery mildew fungi are generally:
A. Obligate biotrophs    B. Obligate saprophytes    C. Soil-borne bacteria   D. Facultative saprophytes
17. Rust diseases of wheat are commonly caused by species of:
A. Fusarium    B. Puccinia    C. Rhizoctonia    D. Pythium
18. Heteroecious rust fungi require:
A. Two different hosts to complete their life cycle    B. Two pathogens on the same host
C. Two environmental conditions    D. Two types of fertilizers
19. Bacteria are classified as:
A. Eukaryotic organisms   B. Prokaryotic organisms   C. Multicellular fungi  D. Obligate parasites
20. Bacterial ooze observed from diseased tissue is considered a:
A. Symptom   B. Sign   C. Physiological disorder   D. Resistance reaction
21. Bacterial leaf blight of rice is caused by:
A. Ralstonia solanacearum  B. Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae
C. Agrobacterium tumefaciens   D. Pseudomonas syringae
22. Ralstonia solanacearum is primarily responsible for:
A. Bacterial wilt   B. Citrus canker   C. Rice blast   D. Wheat rust
23. Crown gall disease is caused by:
A. Xanthomonas oryzae      B. Agrobacterium tumefaciens
C. Ralstonia solanacearu     D. Pseudomonas syringae
24. Agrobacterium causes crown gall mainly through transfer of:
A. RNA    B. T-DNA       C. Ribosomal proteins   D. Fungal spores
25. Citrus canker is characteristically associated with:
A. Root galls   B. Raised corky lesions    C. White powdery growth    D. Vascular browning only
26. Plant viruses are generally:
A. Free-living organisms    B. Obligate intracellular parasites   C. Saprophytic fungi
D. Prokaryotic organisms
27. Tobacco mosaic virus contains:
A. DNA     B. RNA    C. Both DNA and RNA   D. Protein as genetic material
28. A common symptom associated with viral diseases is:
A. Mosaic   B. Sclerotium    C. Bacterial ooze   D. Rust pustules
29. Which insect group is an important vector of many plant viruses?
A. Aphids    B. Termites    C. Earthworms    D. Grasshoppers
30. Mechanical transmission of a plant virus commonly occurs through:
A. Infected plant sap   B. Fertilizer granules   C. Soil nutrients  D. Fungal spores
31. Phytoplasmas are mainly associated with the:
A. Xylem  B. Phloem C. Epidermis  D. Root cortex
32. Phytoplasmas are commonly transmitted by:
A. Leafhoppers   B. Earthworms   C. Fungi   D. Mites only
33. Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus:
A. Heterodera     B. Meloidogyne    C. Pratylenchus   D. Tylenchulus
34. The characteristic symptom of Meloidogyne infection is:
A. Leaf mosaic  B. Root galls    C. Rust pustules  D. Bacterial ooze
35. Plant-parasitic nematodes are generally:
A. Microscopic roundworms    B. Fungi    C. Bacteria   D. Protozoa
36. Disease incidence generally represents the:
A. Degree of tissue damage  B. Proportion of plant units affected
C. Amount of pathogen in soil  D. Number of spores produced
37. Disease severity refers to the:
A. Degree or extent of disease development   B. Number of diseased fields
C. Amount of inoculum in seed   D. Number of vectors present
38. The period between infection and the appearance of symptoms is called the:
A. Latent period    B. Incubation period    C. Survival period   D. Generation period
39. Secondary inoculum is inoculum that:
A. Initiates the first infection   B. Develops from primary infections and causes further infections   C. Remains dormant in seed      D. Is produced only sexually
40. Which environmental condition generally favors many foliar fungal diseases?
A. High relative humidity and prolonged leaf wetness   B. Very low humidity
C. Complete absence of moisture   D. Extremely dry conditions
41. Removal and destruction of diseased plant debris is known as:
A. Inoculation   B. Sanitation   C. Incubation  D. Sporulation
42. Crop rotation is particularly useful for managing pathogens that:
A. Survive in soil or crop residues    B. Are transmitted only by insects
C. Have no survival stage     D. Infect plants only through air
43. Bordeaux mixture is composed mainly of:
A. Copper sulphate and lime  B. Sulphur and urea   C. Zinc sulphate and lime
D. Copper chloride and urea
44. Seed treatment is primarily used to manage:
A. Seed-borne and soil-borne pathogens    B. Viral vectors only
C. Nutrient deficiencies    D. Insect pests only
45. The use of resistant varieties represents:
A. Chemical control     B. Host resistance    C. Physical control      D. Eradication
46. Trichoderma spp. are widely used as:
A. Biological control agents     B. Viral vectors      C. Insecticides      D. Plant-parasitic nematodes
47. A fungicide capable of moving within plant tissues is generally called a:
A. Contact fungicide     B. Systemic fungicide     C. Protective dust    D. Surface disinfectant
48. Integrated Disease Management (IDM) involves:
A. Use of fungicides alone      B. Combining compatible disease-management methods
C. Using resistant varieties alone    D. Avoiding disease monitoring
49. A disease that produces several successive generations of infection during one cropping season is generally called:
A. Monocyclic disease   B. Polycyclic disease    C. Abiotic disease
D. Non-infectious disease
50. The most sustainable approach to plant disease management is generally to:
A. Depend entirely on chemicals     B. Use only biological control    C. Integrate multiple compatible management strategies   D. Avoid preventive measures
